records.name: Lee et al. (2008): monolayer graphene in-plane stiffness (2D)

uncertainty.interpretation: The paper reports a ± value; its statistical type and coverage have not been verified. Do not treat it as a confidence interval, standard deviation, standard error or certified bound.

method.inference: Two-dimensional in-plane elastic stiffness inferred by fitting AFM force–displacement curves with a membrane indentation model; this is a model-dependent experimental summary.
model_assumptions: Clamped isotropic circular membrane under central indentation; the elastic fit uses the point-load approximation in Eq. (2).
Poisson ratio 0.165 is a modeling assumption, not a measured result.

notes: These are stiffness-fit statistics only, not breaking-test sample counts.
The distribution standard deviation 30 N/m is distinct from the reported stiffness uncertainty ±50 N/m; neither statistic is replaced by the other.

gaps: Supporting supplementary material was inaccessible; uncertainty type and coverage have not been verified.
Temperature, atmosphere, humidity and loading rate have not been verified.
No raw-data reanalysis, independent replication, specimen-condition validation or independent scientific review is claimed.

evidence.locator: Science 321 (2008), p. 387 final paragraph (340 ± 50 N/m); p. 386 final paragraph (23 membranes from 2 flakes); p. 387 opening and Fig. 3A discussion (67 fits; mean 342 N/m, standard deviation 30 N/m); p. 386 Eqs. (1)–(2) and membrane-model discussion; p. 385 and Fig. 1 (preparation, monolayer identification and spans).
evidence.verified_as: Reported two-dimensional elastic stiffness and separate fit-distribution statistics; a model-dependent observation rather than a universal elastic bound.

limits: Observational context from one study, not a theoretical or universal material limit, engineering allowable or new executable rule.
This two-dimensional force-per-length quantity must not be identified with a three-dimensional pressure merely by changing unit labels. No thickness conversion is performed.
Matching N/m units do not make in-plane stiffness and breaking strength the same quantity. Material state, dimensionality, quantity, method and stress/strain conventions must also be compatible.
These two records share one study and are not independent confirmations. They cannot be passed to the composite evaluator or overlaid on its volume-fraction sweeps.

The authors infer defect-free behavior in the highly stressed region beneath the tip; this is not independent imaging proof for every entire membrane or a guarantee for macroscopic or processed graphene.

records.name: Lee et al. (2008): monolayer graphene breaking strength (2D)

uncertainty.interpretation: The paper reports a ± value; its statistical type and coverage have not been verified. Do not treat it as a confidence interval, standard deviation, standard error or certified bound.

method.inference: Two-dimensional breaking strength inferred from AFM failure measurements using nonlinear membrane elasticity and finite-element simulation. The constitutive convention is sigma=E2D*epsilon+D2D*epsilon^2 with second Piola–Kirchhoff stress and uniaxial Lagrangian strain; its model maximum is -E2D^2/(4*D2D). These are source-model descriptions, not executable formulas or direct uniform-stress measurements.
model_assumptions: Clamped isotropic circular membrane indented centrally by a finite-radius AFM tip; the failure inference uses nonlinear finite-element modeling and accounts for tip radius, not the point-load approximation used for elastic fitting.
Poisson ratio 0.165 is a modeling assumption, not a measured result.

gaps: Supporting supplementary material was inaccessible; uncertainty type and coverage have not been verified.
Temperature, atmosphere, humidity and loading rate have not been verified.
No raw-data reanalysis, independent replication, specimen-condition validation or independent scientific review is claimed.
Breaking-test sample counts are not verified in this record; the stiffness-fit counts are not transferred to breaking strength.

evidence.locator: Science 321 (2008), p. 388 opening paragraph (42 ± 4 N/m); p. 387 final-column numerical-simulation paragraph (nonlinear finite-element failure inference and tip-radius dependence); p. 386 Eq. (1) and associated nonlinear constitutive and maximum-stress discussion; p. 385 and Fig. 1 (preparation, monolayer identification and spans).
evidence.verified_as: Source-reported model-inferred two-dimensional breaking strength from AFM failure, with the source stress/strain convention retained; not a directly measured uniform tensile stress or universal bound.

limits: Observational context from one study, not a theoretical or universal material limit, engineering allowable or new executable rule.
This two-dimensional force-per-length quantity must not be identified with a three-dimensional pressure merely by changing unit labels. No thickness conversion is performed.
Matching N/m units do not make in-plane stiffness and breaking strength the same quantity. Material state, dimensionality, quantity, method and stress/strain conventions must also be compatible.
These two records share one study and are not independent confirmations. They cannot be passed to the composite evaluator or overlaid on its volume-fraction sweeps.

Breaking strength here depends on the nonlinear constitutive inference and reference stress/strain measures; do not substitute Cauchy stress, engineering stress or a generic three-dimensional tensile strength.

The authors infer defect-free behavior in the highly stressed region beneath the tip; this is not independent imaging proof for every entire membrane or a guarantee for macroscopic or processed graphene.
